description: A stereo brickwall limiter with four milliseconds of lookahead, so the gain is already down before a peak arrives

params.text: Sets how fast the gain returns after a peak, from 1ms to 5 seconds
Sets the ceiling, from -15dB to 7.5dB, on a scale where 0dB is 5V and 7.5dB is about 12V
Sets how fast the gain comes down on a peak, from 0.02ms to 2ms
Multiplies the signal after limiting, from 0dB to 20dB

inputs.text: One side of the stereo pair to be limited
One side of the stereo pair to be limited
Sets the ceiling from its own voltage instead of from the knob: the size of the voltage is read as a level, the knob is moved to match and 0V is taken as -15dB
Patching either sidechain jack switches detection away from the programme, so the gain follows what is here rather than what is being limited
Patching either sidechain jack switches detection away from the programme, so the gain follows what is here rather than what is being limited

outputs.text: That side of the pair after limiting and makeup gain, clamped to ±12V
That side of the pair after limiting and makeup gain, clamped to ±12V

notes: the two sides share one gain, so a peak on either channel ducks both and the stereo image does not shift.
the red lamp lights while the limiter is holding the gain down and the blue lamp while the gain is at unity.
the four columns of lamps are levels: input left, input right, output left and output right, each covering 22.5dB in fifteen steps from green through yellow to red.
mono per side: a polyphonic cable is read as its first channel.
the detector runs at four times the sample rate, so the peak it measures is the one between the samples rather than only the ones on the sample grid.
the threshold jack takes over the knob for as long as it is patched, and the knob is left wherever the jack last put it when the cable is pulled.
menu: Maximizer — adds automatic makeup gain equal to the amount the ceiling is below 0dB, so lowering the threshold makes the signal louder rather than quieter
